title: Sunrise over the VLT
caption: The first light of sunrise over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Sunrise is just beginning over ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory in Chile. One of the VLT's Unit Telescopes stands at the bottom right, lit by the Moon, and farther off two Auxiliary Telescopes point upwards.

The VLT has four 8.2-metre Unit Telescopes and four movable 1.8-metre Auxiliary Telescopes. Working together they form a giant interferometer, known as the Very Large Telescope Interferometer. A complex system of mirrors in underground tunnels combines their light, revealing details up to 16 times finer than a single Unit Telescope can see.

Astronomer Nicolas Blind took the picture during a visit of a few days in December 2012. He recalls a silence so complete that he could hear only the wind, or perhaps a lost bat, and says the clear sky reminded him how small we are and why he chose astronomy.

understand.summary: This is a dawn landscape photograph by Nicolas Blind. The source gives no camera or colour details.
understand.eye: This photograph records ordinary visible light at the start of sunrise, and the source gives no detail on how it was processed.

explore: Paranal enjoys 330 clear nights a year, and ESO describes the VLT as the world's most productive individual ground-based facility. Blind shared the photograph through the Your ESO Pictures Flickr group, which ESO reviews for its Picture of the Week series.
alt: A large telescope enclosure lit by moonlight at lower right, with two smaller telescopes in the distance under a brightening dawn sky.
